title: Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court
summary: The Rome Statute, the treaty creating the International Criminal Court, was concluded at Rome on 17 July 1998. It gave the court jurisdiction over genocide, war crimes, crimes against humanity and aggression. It entered into force on 1 July 2002, with the court based permanently at The Hague.

importance.justification: Founding treaty of the first permanent international criminal court, a major development in international criminal law.

reviewer_note: Sources give 17 July 1998 as the conclusion date; Britannica gives only 1998 and mentions 120 countries adopting it. The UN record lists signature dates up to 2000 and later, so signature dates vary by state.The UN source text is truncated.Hague seat is from Britannica.Wikidata date matches.Aggression's inclusion is stated by Britannica's war crimes entry.The ICC's exact start date is the entry into force on 1 July 2002.Britannica says the court came into existence then.
